source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Existing public labels match all selected Hebrew records in Jeremiah 21–40. The final capture clause at 38:28 remains bound inside that verse; no relabeling performed.

key_decisions.decision: Keeps the deported social groups and the queen mother's specific role.
Uses the same rendering for all three occurrences of shalom to make the shared welfare connection audible.
Preserves the causative dream wording, with the possible direct dreaming sense noted.
Retains 'for Babylon' rather than converting it into seventy years for each exile.
Keeps the plural exiled audience in context and preserves both future and hope without promising individual wealth.
Keeps the consequential shift from 'they' to 'you' rather than harmonizing the audience.
Preserves the fathers' names to distinguish these men from kings of the same names.
Retains the brutal manner of killing and the order of names in the curse.
Follows the read 'one who knows' despite the divided written form; preserves adultery and unauthorized speech.
Keeps the new recipient's identifying designation without inventing its origin.
Preserves the unauthorized sender's own name and all letter recipients while unpacking the long introductory syntax.
Keeps 'madman' within Shemaiah's hostile letter, and retains both devices of confinement with uncertainty noted.
Preserves the hostile description and Jeremiah's hometown.
Retains the letter's quotation of Jeremiah and its repeated settlement commands.
